items.title: Do not error when no environment file is found
items.reason: Canonical discussion for letting `uv run` proceed when a named dotenv file is absent. The report uses `UV_ENV_FILE`; a maintainer suggested a separate default-file setting rather than weakening explicitly requested files.

items.title: [Feature request] add option to allow UV_ENV_FILE to point to non-existing file
items.reason: Tracks the same failure when sharing dotenv configuration across projects with and without a `.env` file. The discussion also proposes a flag to load `.env` only when present.

items.title: Add `env-file` setting for loading environment files in `uv run`
items.reason: Proposes skipping missing files listed in configuration while explicitly keeping missing `--env-file` arguments fatal. It does not implement the requested CLI flag.

related.search_scope: Searched open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged PRs with `gh` for the proposed flag, `--env-file`, `UV_ENV_FILE`, the exact `No environment file found at` diagnostic, and variants for optional or best-effort dotenv loading and `uv run --script`. Followed comments and linked changes: astral-sh/uv#8263 added explicit loading, not an optional CLI path. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#16926 as the primary match because it concerns implicit discovery and persistent opt-in, astral-sh/uv#15806 because it concerns a path containing spaces, and astral-sh/uv#18017 because it concerns an option passed after the script path.

type_reason: The proposed flag and shebang example give a new interface and use case for the same behavior tracked in astral-sh/uv#16672 and astral-sh/uv#9270: load the named dotenv file if present and run without it if absent. The checkout's integration test expects exit code 2 for a missing file passed to `--env-file`, and the report does not describe a regression.
summary: astral-sh/uv#16672 is the canonical discussion for optional dotenv loading, and astral-sh/uv#9270 also discusses a flag. astral-sh/uv#22385 proposes optional files in configuration only.
draft_response: `uv run --env-file` treats the named file as required. We're discussing opt-in loading that skips missing files in astral-sh/uv#16672. Please add your shebang example there: it shows why a CLI flag would be useful even if a config-file option were available. For now, a shell wrapper can pass `--env-file .env` when the file exists and `--no-env-file` otherwise.
